versions.runtimeLabel: TeaVM 0.13.1 (frozen release; its WASI backend was removed in 0.14.0). NOT the JVM: not comparable to the matrix Java cells
versions.frontEnd: javac --release 25 (JDK 25.0.4.1, Debian openjdk-25-jdk-headless; TeaVM 0.13.1 rejects class file major version 70, so the matrix Java 26 cannot be used)

transforms: none on the sources; the same class files (one front-end compile per benchmark) feed both TeaVM backends
asymmetries: primary: the native column is TeaVM's C backend + LLVM clang -O2; the wasm column is TeaVM's own wasm emitter (no LLVM, no binaryen pass) + Cranelift, so the ratio mixes backend quality with the wasm cost

TeaVM runtime and GC differ per backend: the C backend uses its C runtime (memory.c, glibc) and the wasi backend its own Java-written/wasm runtime with linear memory sized by --min-heap/--max-heap; same heap flags on both
the wasm backend runs without wasm exception-handling instructions (--wasm-use-exceptions not set); the C backend uses its own mechanism
front end is javac 25 not the matrix Java 26, and TeaVM replaces the JDK class library with its own classlib: no HotSpot, no JIT, no JVM GC anywhere
TeaVM 0.13.1 output is not byte-reproducible: two builds of the same Dockerfile gave identical tak.wasm but a different bigint.wasm of the same size (cause not investigated)

teavmOptionSensitivity.how: Java only, 6 benchmarks, same TeaVM options on both backends (teavm -t C then clang 23.1.0 -O2; teavm -t wasi then wasmtime 50), qemu insn differentials, every cell gated
teavmOptionSensitivity.reading: the heap size barely matters (-1.2%, binary-trees only); a lower -O raises the ratio by 20 to 31%, almost all through k-nucleotide and sha256, so the shipped -O 3 is the setting most favourable to wasm among those tested
